close_reason: Policy decision (c) committed: raw DER byte comparison for TeletexString; no T.61→Unicode transcoding. Docs updated in pkix-path/src/lib.rs.
description:
## Why

Subset of PKIX-l63j epic. RFC 4518 §1.6 punts on T.61 transcoding ('implementation-defined'). `der::asn1::TeletexString` exists in der 0.7.10 but treats T.61 as ASCII/Latin-1 — not real T.61 multi-byte decoding.

## What

Decide policy:
- (a) implement ISO 6937 subset like OpenSSL does (~50 lines of mapping table)
- (b) strict-reject T61String DNs in strict modes; document as ASCII-fallback only otherwise

Recommend (b) initially per parent bead. Implement and update limitation docs.

## Acceptance

- See parent PKIX-l63j acceptance.
notes: Resolved by policy decision: option (c) — commit to status quo. pkix-path uses raw DER byte comparison for TeletexString AVAs and does not transcode T.61 to Unicode. Rationale: OpenSSL/NSS/GnuTLS use mutually incompatible vendor T.61 tables; adopting any of them would silently diverge from the others. Byte-equality is fail-closed and satisfies RFC 5280 §4.1.2.4 well-formed issuer/subject DN reuse. Docs updated at pkix-path/src/lib.rs (any_to_str_bytes rustdoc, names_match rustdoc, crate-level Limitations section).
title: pkix-path: TeletexString policy decision (strict-reject or ISO 6937 mapping)
